w: A 2,061m pass between the Eiger and Lauberhorn, crossed by the Wengernalp Railway linking Grindelwald to Lauterbrunnen via Wengen. Its station is also the lower terminus of the Jungfrau Railway, tunnelling to Jungfraujoch, Europe's highest rail point. The Jungfrau Marathon finishes here each September.
s: Junction of two railways under the Eiger

w: Above the Jungfraujoch station, an elevator bored through rock climbs to this observatory at 3,571m, one of the highest in the world and the second-highest observation deck in Switzerland. Its open deck looks across at the Jungfrau, Monch and Eiger, from a summit named for the rock it sits on.

w: An 8-hectare alpine lake at 2,265m near First, split unevenly by a natural dam into two basins six metres apart in height. Its mirror-still water and jagged Bernese Oberland skyline made it famous well beyond hiking circles: Gmail used the view as a mountain-themed background image in 2013.
s: The alpine lake that became a Gmail wallpaper

w: At 4,042m, the second-highest summit wholly within the canton of Bern, tied by a ridge to its taller neighbour the Schreckhorn. Ringed by the Lauteraargletscher, Strahlegg-Gletscher and Obers Ischmeer, it lies about 10km southeast of Grindelwald. First climbed on 8 August 1842 by Pierre Jean Edouard Desor's party.
s: First climbed in 1842, tied to the Schreckhorn

w: A cable-car station, the Firstbahn, on the slopes of the Schwarzhorn above Grindelwald, better known today as a hiking hub than a summit. The Bachalpsee lies just beyond it, and First anchors the classic high route from Schynige Platte over the Faulhorn to First - one of the Bernese Oberland's signature ridge walks.
s: Cable car hub above the Bachalpsee
